text:
lucy: quick heads-up — ran an overnight perf sweep against staging-serving with the new kernel-routing change. saw repeated p99 spikes when concurrency > 1.5k and KV cache churn is high.

sam: ugh. numbers?

lucy: p95 steady ~45ms, p99 up from 210ms -> 780ms on many hosts. throughput unchanged. correlates with KV_EVICT bursts.

maya: any change in microbatch sizing? we pushed default mb_target=16 last week.

lucy: yes MB target 16. i compared MB=8/12/16/32 across the same load. MB=12 gave best p99 vs throughput tradeoff during eviction waves. MB=32 amplified tail.

ejan (perf-bot): automatic profile uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/2005002468 (summary attached)

maya: can you paste the hotspot?

lucy: pasted snippet:
```
KV_EVICT: count=1420, window=10s
memcpy_ms: p95=6 p99=48
kernel_fallbacks: 62 events
cpu_stall_us: p99=320
overall_p99_ms: 780
```

sam: kernel_fallbacks = suspicious. which kernels were selected before fallback?

lucy: default path picks fast-quantized kernels for short seqs. when cache eviction causes repeated KV misses we see longer sequences (recompute), which triggers a path that isn't JIT'd for those shapes -> fallback to slower kernels + memcpy.

ejan (perf-bot): flame shows hot path in KV serialization and non-coalesced memcpy.

maya: sounds like two amplifiers: eviction causing longer compute + microbatching exposing memcpy hot loops.

jordan: do we have an easy experiment to separate kernel routing mischoice vs pure cache pressure?

lucy: yes. two quick ones: 1) force kernel-routing to prefer robust kernel (less specialized) for 5m and run the same load. 2) keep current routing but reduce MB target to 12 and increase schedule_coalesce window to 8ms.

sam: can we A/B these on 2 nodes first? don't want cluster-wide risk.

lucy: scheduled a canary on staging-2 (done). initial 10m run: with robust kernel policy p99 dropped to ~260ms during similar eviction bursts. throughput -2.5%.

maya: that's promising. MB=12 results?

lucy: MB=12 without changing kernels gave p99 ~320ms and throughput -1%. combined robust-kernel + MB=12 -> p99 ~240ms and throughput -3%.

ejan (perf-bot): note: when MB decreases we see more KV lookup QPS which slightly increases eviction rate in small hosts.

jordan: oh nice catch. so smaller MB reduces tail by avoiding large batch-induced scheduling delays, but it increases load on KV which can counteract.

sam: what's the rollback plan if this regresses in prod after enabling robust kernel route?

lucy: feature flag rollout with 10% -> 50% -> 100% and automated revert if p99 increases by >20% or error rate >0.5%. also we can pin MB target per-customer route.

maya: do we want to tweak the eviction policy too? maybe prefer LRU with weight on token-access-time instead of pure frequency for short-lived hotsets.

lucy: prototyped a 'sticky prefix' heuristic that gives short-lived hot keys a short TTL bump. in sims it reduced eviction storms by ~18% under bursty QPS.

ejan (perf-bot): simulation log: sticky_prefix reduced eviction_rate from 0.42 -> 0.34 per-window.

jordan: can you drop the simulation script or command so I can run locally?

lucy: run: 
```
python tools/sim_cache.py --workload traces/2026-02-burst.json --policy sticky_prefix --window 10
```
lucy: note: the sim uses sampled traces; real world interaction with kernel routing still matters.

sam: action items?

lucy: 1) enable robust-kernel route under flag on prod canary (sam) 2) test MB target=12 on dedicated pool (maya) 3) run sticky_prefix A/B in staging KV on Wednesday (jordan) 4) perf-bot to auto-collect flame and p95/p99 every 5m during rollout (evan)

sam: pinging infra for canary slot. @evan can you wire perf-bot alert for +20% p99?

ev an (typo intentional?)

ev an: on it, will add grafana alert and slack webhook.

maya: one more ask — please capture kernel-selection trace at TRACE level for 30s during canary. we need to see exact fallback causes.

lucy: ack. enabling TRACE for 30s window.

jordan: LGTM. thanks for triage. feels actionable. :thumbsup:

lucy: will post short follow-up with final numbers after the 4h canary. (reacts :eyes:)
